lesson.title: Prisms and pyramids
lesson.body: A prism has two equal bases joined by rectangles. A pyramid has one base and triangles that meet at a point.

lesson.title: Cubes and boxes
lesson.body: A cube and a rectangular prism both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. A cube's edges are all equal; a box has 4 edges of each of its three lengths.

lesson.title: Add the faces
lesson.body: Surface area is the total area of all the faces. A cube has 6 equal squares; a box has 3 pairs of matching rectangles.

lesson.title: Open boxes
lesson.body: A box with no lid has only 5 faces: the bottom and the four sides.

lesson.title: Length × width × height
lesson.body: Volume is the space inside, counted in cubes. A box 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm holds 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cubes of 1 cm³.

lesson.title: Working back
lesson.body: If you know the volume and two edges, divide: a 60 cm³ box that is 5 cm by 4 cm is 60 ÷ 20 = 3 cm high.

lesson.title: Volume and capacity
lesson.body: Volume is measured in cubic units like cm³ and m³; capacity, how much liquid fits, in litres and millilitres.

lesson.title: 1 litre is 1000 cm³
lesson.body: A cube 10 cm on each side holds exactly 1 litre: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 cm³. So 1 mL is 1 cm³.

lesson.title: Volume, then litres
lesson.body: To find how much a tank holds, find its volume in cm³, then divide by 1000 to get litres.
